stem: For her class project, Meera makes a chart of the planets in our solar system. Which statement about the planets is correct?

options.text: The Moon is a planet because it is round and moves around the Sun.
Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars are the inner planets; Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune are the outer planets.
All eight planets are large balls made mostly of gases.
The planets can be ordered by their brightness in the night sky, starting with Venus.

teacher.key_rationale: B correctly states the inner-outer grouping: Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars are the inner (rocky) planets and Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune are the large gaseous outer planets. A is wrong because the Moon revolves around Earth, not the Sun, so it is not a planet. C is wrong because the four inner planets are rocky, not gaseous. D is wrong because planet order is set by distance from the Sun, not brightness.
